cases.sentence: Пьер, со времени исчезновения своего из дома, уже ___ жил на пустой квартире покойного Баздеева.
cases.explain: «второй день» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: For the last two days, ever since leaving home, Pierre had been living in the empty house of his deceased benefactor, Osip Bazdéev. This is how it happened.

cases.sentence: Проснувшись на ___ после своего возвращения в Москву и свидания с графом Растопчиным, Пьер долго не мог понять того, где он находился и чего от него хотели.
cases.explain: «другой день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: When he woke up on the morning after his return to Moscow and his interview with Count Rostopchín, he could not for some time make out where he was and what was expected of him. When he was informed that among others awaiting him in his reception room there was a Frenchman who had brought a letter from his wife, the Countess Elèna Vasílievna, he felt suddenly overcome by that sense of confusion and hopelessness to which he was apt to succumb. He felt that everything was now at an end, all was in confusion and crumbling to pieces, that nobody was right or wrong, the future held nothing, and there was no escape from this position. Smiling unnaturally and muttering to himself, he first sat down on the sofa in an attitude of despair, then rose, went to the door of the reception room and peeped through the crack, returned flourishing his arms, and took up a book. His majordomo came in a second time to say that the Frenchman who had brought the letter from the countess was very anxious to see him if only for a minute, and that someone from Osip Alexéevich Bazdéev’s widow had called to ask Pierre to take charge of her husband’s books, as she herself was leaving for the country.

cases.sentence: Пьер прошел во всю длину коридора до лестницы и, морщась и растирая лоб обеими руками, спустился до ___.
cases.explain: «первой площадки» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: But as soon as the man had left the room Pierre took up his hat which was lying on the table and went out of his study by the other door. There was no one in the passage. He went along the whole length of this passage to the stairs and, frowning and rubbing his forehead with both hands, went down as far as the first landing. The hall porter was standing at the front door. From the landing where Pierre stood there was a second staircase leading to the back entrance. He went down that staircase and out into the yard. No one had seen him. But there were some carriages waiting, and as soon as Pierre stepped out of the gate the coachmen and the yard porter noticed him and raised their caps to him. When he felt he was being looked at he behaved like an ostrich which hides its head in a bush in order not to be seen: he hung his head and quickening his pace went down the street.

cases.translation: He hired the first cab he met and told the driver to go to the Patriarch’s Ponds, where the widow Bazdéev’s house was.

cases.sentence: Извозчик рассказал ему, что ___ разбирают в Кремле оружие, и что на завтрашний народ выгоняют весь за Трехгорную заставу, и что там будет большое сражение.
cases.explain: «нынешний день» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: The man told him that arms were being distributed today at the Krémlin and that tomorrow everyone would be sent out beyond the Three Hills gates and a great battle would be fought there.

cases.sentence: Приехав на ___, Пьер отыскал дом Баздеева, в котором он давно не бывал.
cases.explain: «Патриаршие пруды» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Having reached the Patriarch’s Ponds Pierre found the Bazdéevs’ house, where he had not been for a long time past. He went up to the gate. Gerásim, that sallow beardless old man Pierre had seen at Torzhók five years before with Osip Alexéevich, came out in answer to his knock.

cases.sentence: Герасим, тот самый желтый ___, которого Пьер видел пять лет тому назад в Торжке с Иосифом Алексеевичем, вышел на его стук.

cases.sentence: — Пожалуйте, милости просим, братец покойника, — царство небесное, — Макар Алексеевич, остались, да как изволите знать, они в слабости, — сказал ___.
cases.explain: «старый слуга» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Be so good as to step in. Makár Alexéevich, the brother of my late master—may the kingdom of heaven be his—has remained here, but he is in a weak state as you know,” said the old servant.

cases.sentence: Высокий, плешивый ___ в халате, с красным носом, в калошах на босу ногу, стоял в передней: увидав Пьера, он сердито пробормотал что-то и ушел в коридор.
cases.explain: «старый человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Yes, yes, I know. Let us go in …” said Pierre and entered the house. A tall, bald-headed old man with a red nose, wearing a dressing gown and with galoshes on his bare feet, stood in the anteroom. On seeing Pierre he muttered something angrily and went away along the passage.

cases.sentence: — ___ были, а теперь, как изволите видеть, ослабели, — сказал Герасим.
cases.explain: «Большого ума» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “He was a very clever man but has now grown quite feeble, as your honor sees,” said Gerásim. “Will you step into the study?” Pierre nodded. “As it was sealed up so it has remained, but Sófya Danílovna gave orders that if anyone should come from you they were to have the books.”

cases.sentence: Пьер вошел в тот самый ___, в который он еще при жизни благодетеля входил с таким трепетом.
cases.explain: «мрачный кабинет» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Pierre went into that gloomy study which he had entered with such trepidation in his benefactor’s lifetime. The room, dusty and untouched since the death of Osip Alexéevich was now even gloomier.

cases.sentence: Это были подлинные ___ с примечаниями и объяснениями благодетеля.
cases.explain: «шотландские акты» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Gerásim opened one of the shutters and left the room on tiptoe. Pierre went round the study, approached the cupboard in which the manuscripts were kept, and took out what had once been one of the most important, the holy of holies of the order. This was the authentic Scotch Acts with Bazdéev’s notes and explanations. He sat down at the dusty writing table, and, having laid the manuscripts before him, opened them out, closed them, finally pushed them away, and resting his head on his hand sank into meditation.

cases.sentence: Мне нужно ___ и пистолет, — сказал Пьер, неожиданно покраснев.
cases.explain: «крестьянское платье» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No, but I want something else. I want peasant clothes and a pistol,” said Pierre, unexpectedly blushing.

cases.sentence: Герасим с привычкой слуги, видавшего много ___ на своем веку, принял переселение Пьера без удивления и, казалось, был доволен тем, что ему было кому услуживать.
cases.explain: «странных вещей» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Gerásim, being a servant who in his time had seen many strange things, accepted Pierre’s taking up his residence in the house without surprise, and seemed pleased to have someone to wait on. That same evening—without even asking himself what they were wanted for—he procured a coachman’s coat and cap for Pierre, and promised to get him the pistol next day. Makár Alexéevich came twice that evening shuffling along in his galoshes as far as the door and stopped and looked ingratiatingly at Pierre. But as soon as Pierre turned toward him he wrapped his dressing gown around him with a shamefaced and angry look and hurried away. It was when Pierre (wearing the coachman’s coat which Gerásim had procured for him and had disinfected by steam) was on his way with the old man to buy the pistol at the Súkharev market that he met the Rostóvs.
